verdict: Strong 6.2L L86 V8 block but the 2017 truck is dragged down by the 8L90 8-speed (harsh shifts, torque converter shudder) and AFM/DFM lifter failures; CR rates 2017 below average. At 191k miles it is on borrowed time for transmission/valvetrain.
major_issues: 8L90 shudder/harsh shift, valve body/solenoid issues (flush or TC replacement ~$500-1,500; rebuild ~$3,500-5,000+; GM class-action noted). AFM lifter collapse/ticking ($2,000-4,500, often 100k-200k). Rear diff/transfer case (4WD) leaks, brake line/caliper corrosion, infotainment/electrical glitches, 6 NHTSA recalls.
risk_reason: 191k miles on a full-size truck with an 8L90 and AFM lifters; either failure alone exceeds $1,000, plus tires/brakes/4WD service costs. Parts are pricey.
inspect_today: Cold start: listen for lifter tick/misfire (P0300, P0301-08, check for DFM/AFM codes). Test drive through all gears for shudder at 25-45 mph, flares, harsh 1-2/2-3 shifts; check trans fluid color/smell. Scan for stored codes/readiness monitors. Check 4WD engage, transfer case/diff leaks, oil level and condition, rust on brake lines/frame, tire wear, leaks at rear main.

verdict: Average-to-mediocre subcompact; 1.4 turbo (LUV) is cheap to run but has coolant, PCV and water pump/thermostat weak points. RepairPal 4.0/5 overall, $536/yr.
major_issues: Coolant leaks (water pump/thermostat housing, plastic fittings, $400-900), turbo/PCV/oil-cooler seal issues ($500-1,500), cooling fan failure, 6-speed auto issues, timing chain stretch occasionally past 120k, oil consumption in some cases.
risk_reason: 142k miles; cheap car, but turbo/coolant/transmission repairs can pass $1,000 and the car's value is low.
inspect_today: Check coolant level/color, residue around water pump and thermostat housing, oil in coolant or milky cap, overheating behavior, fan operation, turbo whine/smoke, oil level, auto trans shift quality (6T35), cold-start chain rattle, scan codes.

verdict: Naturally aspirated 1.8 (Ecotec) is simpler and generally more durable than the turbo; solid for the class but cars at 178-184k are old. RepairPal $536/yr.
major_issues: Water pump/thermostat leaks, cooling fan failure, motor mounts, 6T35 automatic shifting/mount issues (verify transmission; $2,000-3,500 if bad), timing chain wear is less common, sensor/EVAP issues. Note: 1.8 is not in the Sonic hatch for flex fuel in many sources; confirm.
risk_reason: Engine is simple, but both cars are 178-184k miles; automatic transmission, water pump, struts/brakes could together or singly push past $1,000.
inspect_today: Check transmission shift behavior and fluid, coolant leaks at water pump/thermostat, engine oil level (consumption), motor mounts, suspension noises, CV boots, scan for codes, A/C operation, cooling fan operation, signs of overheating.

verdict: Roomy but below-average reliability (RepairPal 3.0/5, 22nd of 26 midsize SUVs). 3.6L LLT timing chain stretch is the headline risk at 80-150k; 6-speed auto and AWD components also costly.
major_issues: Timing chain stretch/P0008-P0017 ($1,500-4,000, onset 80-120k), 6T75 transmission/valve body and torque converter issues ($1,500-4,000), water pump/oil leaks, power steering rack/assist, AWD rear differential/PTU service, oil consumption.
risk_reason: Both cars are at 144k, squarely in the timing chain window, and a family-hauling 3-row with AWD; one chain or transmission fault exceeds $1,000.
inspect_today: Cold start for chain rattle; scan for P0008/P0009/P0016/P0017/P0299; check oil level and sludge under the cap; verify service history (oil changes every 5k); trans shift quality and fluid; AWD PTU/rear diff leaks; check coolant and steering noise; check recalls (VIN).

verdict: Average small crossover; the 1.4 turbo has recurring coolant loss (turbo coolant lines/seals, diverter, head gasket in 2019 complaints) once past ~100k miles.
major_issues: Coolant loss from turbo lines/seals ($1,000-1,500 turbo job; ~$1,200 lines+oil feed), coolant ingestion/head gasket (CarComplaints 2019), water pump/thermostat, 6T35 transmission issues, PCV/oil consumption, rear suspension noises.
risk_reason: Mileages 95k, 113k and 148k; the 148k 2019 is most exposed to coolant/turbo repair. The 95k 2015 is lowest risk but is a 2015 with age.
inspect_today: Check coolant level and residue, pressure-test hoses if possible, check for oil in coolant, turbo whine/smoke, overheating, CEL codes, transmission shifting, PCV/oil leaks, suspension and brake wear, A/C; ask about coolant top-ups.

verdict: Pentastar 3.6 is the sturdier Durango engine; issues are oil filter housing leaks, rocker arm tick, TIPM electrical and 8HP/ZF-based AWD systems. Dodge brand average annual repair about $634 (RepairPal).
major_issues: Oil filter housing/cooler leaks ($900-1,200), rocker arm/lifter tick ($900-2,500, 80-130k), TIPM faults ($650-1,200), water pump, transmission/AWD transfer case issues, cylinder head cracking on early (pre-2014) 3.6 mainly.
risk_reason: Listed A-010 (38,857 mi) is low-risk. B-016 at 237,888 mi is well past typical life and has High risk; VIN/mileage data should be verified. Overall mixed: A-010 Low, B-016 High.
inspect_today: B-016: listen for rocker/lifter tick, check oil leaks at filter housing (valley), coolant, trans shifting, AWD operation, scan for misfire, TIPM faults, suspension; verify odometer. A-010: check for accident/auction condition, title history, remaining warranty status, tires and brakes.

verdict: Hemi 5.7 is strong but prone to MDS lifter/cam failure and exhaust manifold bolts; thirsty and costly at 180-200k, with Dodge-typical electrical issues.
major_issues: MDS lifter/camshaft failure ($2,200-7,500, 70-110k+), exhaust manifold bolt breakage ($500-1,500), valve seat failure, TIPM ($650-1,200), 5-speed/8-speed transmission wear, AWD transfer case, oil consumption.
risk_reason: 182k and 199k miles on a Hemi: lifter/cam risk, brakes, transmission and AWD service make a $1,000+ repair likely.
inspect_today: Cold start ticking (lifter/exhaust manifold leak), scan misfire codes P0300-series, check oil level/condition, exhaust manifold bolts, trans shift quality, transfer case fluid/noise, coolant leaks, TIPM electrical glitches, rust on subframe/brake lines.

verdict: Cheap to buy and fix, kid-friendly, and the 3.6 Pentastar with 6-speed is mostly sturdy; weak points are oil filter housing leaks, rocker arm tick, TIPM and sliding door/electrical items. At 126k it is mid-life.
major_issues: Oil filter housing/cooler leak ($900-1,200), rocker arm tick ($900-2,500), TIPM faults ($650-1,200), 62TE transmission shift issues, power sliding door/liftgate faults, wheel bearings and suspension wear.
risk_reason: 126k is lowish for the engine, but oil housing/rocker or TIPM issue could cross $1,000; many parts are cheap, so most single failures stay under it.
inspect_today: Check for oil leaks under valley/filter housing, cold-start tick, trans shift quality and fluid, scan for codes, TIPM symptoms (random electrics, no-start), both sliding doors and liftgate operation, A/C, tires/brakes, check stow-n-go seats and recalls.
